purpose: Engineering baseline to exercise the research workflow (dataset -> factor -> chronological backtest with costs -> recorded run -> result page). Not evidence that the rule is effective.
signal: position target = 1 (long) if factor > 0 at the close, else 0 (cash). Missing factor (warm-up) = cash.

execution.price: OPEN of the next trading day in the dataset
execution.rule: A signal formed at the close of day t is executed at the open of day t+1; it never trades at the close it was computed on.
execution.return_accounting: Day t+1 return = (1 + p_old*(open/prev_close - 1)) * (1 - cost) * (1 + p_new*(close/open - 1)) - 1, where p_old is the position held overnight and p_new the position after the open trade.

price_series.dividend_note: The a1/a0 ratio changes near quarterly ex-dividend dates, so a1 appears to include cash-dividend adjustment, but the vendor method is undocumented: results are labelled adjusted price returns, not total returns.

costs.definition: cost = bps/10000 * turnover; turnover = |p_new - p_old| as a fraction of NAV traded at the open (a full switch long->cash or cash->long is 1.0, counted once).
costs.nature: engineering assumption, not a broker fee schedule

cash_return.note: No risk-free yield credited to cash; Sharpe uses rf = 0.

benchmark: Buy-and-hold of the same series with the same accounting: long from the first tradable open after warm-up (entry turnover 1.0 charged under each cost scenario), no further trades.
segment_rule: One continuous simulation; each segment's metrics use only that segment's daily returns, with NAV rebased to 1 at the segment start. The rule has no fitted parameters, so segments are reported separately rather than used for selection.
selection_rule: All cost scenarios and all segments are saved and shown; no scenario or interval is selected after seeing results.
